source_text: Περὶ μὲν οὖν σωφροσύνης τοσοῦτον εἶπεν· ,,Ὅς ἂν ἐμβλέψῃ γυναικὶ πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτῆς, ἤδη ἐμοίχευσε τῇ καρδίᾳ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ“. Καί· ,,Εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτόν· συμφέρει γάρ σοι μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἢ μετὰ τῶν δύο πεμφθῆναι εἰς τὸ αἰώνιον πῦρ“. Καί· ,,Ὃς γαμεῖ ἀπολελυμένην ἀφ᾿ ἑτέρου ἀνδρός, μοιχᾶται“. Καί· ,,Εἰσί τινες οἵτινες εὐνουχίσθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, εἰσὶ δὲ οἵ ἐγεννήθησαν εὐνοῦχοι, εἰσὶ δὲ οἵ εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν· πλήν οὐ πάντες τοῦτο χωροῦσιν“. Ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ νόμῳ ἀνθρωπίνῳ διγαμίας ποιούμενοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ τῷ· ἡμετέρῳ διδασκάλῳ εἰσί, καὶ οἱ προσβλέποντες γυναικὶ πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτῆς· οὐ γὰρ μόνον ὁ μοιχεύων ἔργῳ ἐκβέβληται παρ᾿ αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ μοιχεῦσαι βουλόμενος, ὡς οὐ τῶν ἔργων φανερῶν μόνον τῷ θεῷ ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἐνθυμημάτων. Καὶ πολλοί τινες καὶ πολλαὶ ἑξηκοντοῦται καὶ ἑβδομηκοντοῦται, οἵ ἐκ παίδων ἐμαθητεύθησαν τῷ Χριστῷ, ἄφθοροι διαμένουσι· καὶ εὔχομαι κατὰ πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων τοιούτους δεῖξαι. Τί γὰρ καὶ λέγομεν τὸ ἀναρίθμητον πλῆθος τῶν ἐξ ἀκολασίας μεταβαλόντων καὶ ταῦτα μαθόντων; οὐ γὰρ τοὺς δικαίους οὐδὲ τοὺς σώφρονας εἰς μετάνοιαν ἐκάλεσεν ὁ Χριστός, ἀλλὰ τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς καὶ ἀκολάστους καὶ ἀδίκους. Εἶπε δὲ οὕτως· ,,Οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν“. Θέλει γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος τὴν μετάνοιαν τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ ἢ τὴν κόλασιν αὐτοῦ. Περὶ δὲ τοῦ στέργειν ἅπαντας ταῦτα ἐδίδαξεν· ,,Εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τί καινὸν ποιεῖτε; καὶ γὰρ οἱ πόρνοι τοῦτο ποιοῦσιν. Ἐγὼ δὲ ὑμῖν λέγω· Εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς μισοῦντας ὑμᾶς καὶ εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμῖν καὶ εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς“. Εἰς δὲ τὸ κοινωνεῖν τοῖς δεομένοις καὶ μηδὲν πρὸς δόξαν ποιεῖν ταῦτα ἔφη· ,,Παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντι δίδοτε καὶ τὸν βουλόμενον δανείσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῆτε. Εἰ γὰρ δανείζετε παρ᾿ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν, τί καινὸν ποιεῖτε; τοῦτο καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ποιοῦσιν. Ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ θησαυρίζητε ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει καὶ λῃσταὶ διορύσσουσι· θησαυρίζετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει. Τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος, ἂν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ, τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσῃ; ἢ τί δώσει αὐτῆς ἀντάλλαγμα; θησαυρίζετε οὖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει“. Καί· ,,Γίνεσθε δὲ χρηστοὶ καὶ οἰκτίρμονες, ὡς καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν χρηστός ἐστι καὶ οἰκτίρμων, καὶ τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ ἁμαρτωλοὺς καὶ δικαίους καὶ πονηρούς. Μὴ μεριμνᾶτε δὲ τί φάγητε ἢ τί ἐνδύσησθε. Οὐχ ὑμεῖς τῶν πετεινῶν καὶ τῶν θηρίων διαφέρετε; καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτά. Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε τί φάγητε ἢ τί ἐνδύσησθε· οἶδε γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι τούτων χρείαν ἔχετε. Ζητεῖτε δὲ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν. Ὅπου γὰρ ὁ θησαυρός ἐστιν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ὁ νοῦς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου“. Καί· ,,Μὴ ποιῆτε ταῦτα πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς“.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, concerning self-control, He said this: 'Whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart before God.' And: 'If your right eye causes you to stumble, cut it out; for it is better for you to enter the kingdom of heaven with one eye than to be thrown into eternal fire with two eyes.' And: 'Whoever marries a woman divorced from another man commits adultery.' And: 'There are some who have been made eunuchs by men, and there are some who were born eunuchs, and there are some who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven; but not all can accept this.' Just as those who remarry according to human law are considered sinners by our Teacher, so also are those who look at a woman with desire; for not only is the one who commits adultery in deed rejected by Him, but also the one who desires to commit adultery, since God is aware not only of outward actions but also of thoughts. And many men and women, sixty and seventy years old, who were disciples of Christ from childhood, remain pure; and I pray that such people may be found among all humanity. For what can we say about the countless number of people who have changed from a life of debauchery and learned these things? For Christ did not call the righteous or the self-controlled to repentance, but the ungodly, the debauched, and the unjust. He said: 'I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.' For the heavenly Father desires the repentance of the sinner rather than his punishment. Now, concerning loving everyone, He taught this: 'If you love those who love you, what are you doing that is remarkable? Even the prostitutes do this. But I tell you: pray for your enemies and love those who hate you and bless those who curse you and pray for those who mistreat you.' And concerning sharing with those in need and not doing these things for show, He said: 'Give to everyone who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you. For if you lend to those from whom you expect to receive, what are you doing that is remarkable? Even the tax collectors do this. But do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moth and rust destroy and thieves break in; store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys. For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world but lose his own soul? Or what can he give in exchange for his soul? Therefore, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys.' And: 'Be kind and merciful, just as your Father is kind and merciful, and He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good and the wicked. Do not worry about what you will eat or what you will wear. Are you not different from the birds and the beasts? And God feeds them. Therefore, do not worry about what you will eat or what you will wear; for your heavenly Father knows that you need these things. But seek the kingdom of heaven, and all these things will be added to you. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be.' And: 'Do not do these things to be seen by men; for if you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.'

pass_b_english: Concerning self-control, He taught: 'Whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart before God' (Matt 5:27–28); 'If your right eye causes you to stumble, cut it out, for it is better for you to enter the kingdom of heaven with one eye than to be thrown into eternal fire with two' (Matt 5:29–30); 'Whoever marries a woman divorced from another man commits adultery' (Matt 5:31–32); and 'There are those made eunuchs by men, those born eunuchs, and those who make themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven, though not all can accept this' (Matt 19:12). Just as those who remarry by human law are counted sinners by our Teacher, so are those who look on a woman with desire; for not only is the adulterer in deed rejected, but also the one who wishes to commit adultery, since God discerns not only outward deeds but also inward thoughts. Many men and women, now sixty or seventy years old, discipled to Christ from childhood, remain pure; I pray that such may be found in every kind of people. For what shall we say of the countless multitudes who turned from debauchery and learned these things? Christ did not call the righteous or the self-controlled to repentance, but the ungodly, the debauched, and the unjust: 'I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance' (Luke 5:32). The heavenly Father desires the sinner's repentance rather than his punishment.

Concerning love for all, He taught: 'If you love those who love you, what is remarkable in that? Even the prostitutes do the same' (Matt 5:46). 'But I say to you: Pray for your enemies, love those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you' (Matt 5:44). Concerning sharing with the needy and doing nothing for show, He said: 'Give to everyone who asks, and do not turn away the one who wants to borrow' (Matt 5:42); 'If you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what is remarkable? Even tax collectors do that' (Luke 6:34). 'Do not store up treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy and thieves break in; store up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys' (Matt 6:19–20). 'What does it profit a person to gain the whole world yet lose his soul? Or what can he give in exchange for his soul?' (Matt 16:26). Therefore, store up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys. 'Be kind and merciful, just as your Father is kind and merciful, causing His sun to rise on the evil and the good' (Matt 5:45; Luke 6:36). 'Do not worry about what you will eat or wear. Are you not worth more than birds and beasts? God feeds them. So do not worry; your heavenly Father knows you need these things. Seek first the kingdom of heaven, and all these will be added to you. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also' (Matt 6:25–33). 'Do not do these things to be seen by men; otherwise you have no reward from your Father in heaven' (Matt 6:1).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the nuances of the distinction between outward actions and inward thoughts (ἐνθυμημάτων). All scripture citations in Pass B correctly identify the source material alluded to in the Greek. Pass A provides a faithful continuous translation, and Pass B provides a faithful segmented translation with appropriate citations.
